title: Modi Unleashes Rs 9,400 Crore Blitz on Telangana
excerpt: India's first PM MITRA textile park, a smart industrial city, and major rail upgrades land in one historic visit to Hyderabad.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi touched down in Hyderabad on May 10 to inaugurate, dedicate, and lay the foundation stones for development projects worth approximately Rs 9,400 crore — his first visit to Telangana since beginning his third term in office.

**What Modi launched:**
The crown jewel of the day was the PM MITRA Kakatiya Mega Textile Park in Warangal — India's first fully functional PM MITRA Park, built at an estimated cost of Rs 1,700 crore and spread across 1,327 acres. Once fully operational, the park is projected to generate over 24,400 jobs, with 2,000 workers already on the floor. The park operationalises the Centre's '5F' vision: Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign.

**Why this reshapes Telangana's economy:**
Modi also laid the foundation stone for the Zaheerabad Industrial Area in Sangareddy district — a 3,245-acre smart industrial township under the Hyderabad-Nagpur Industrial Corridor designed to attract nearly Rs 10,000 crore in investment and employ up to 1.74 lakh people. Railway infrastructure worth Rs 1,535 crore was dedicated separately, including 118 km of the Kazipet-Vijayawada multi-tracking project to ease congestion on the Grand Trunk corridor. The Prime Minister also handed over Sindhu Hospital, a 1,500-bed cancer-focused super-speciality institution with 29 operation theatres, to the nation.

**What to watch next:**
With BJP eyeing Telangana in the next state election cycle, watch whether the Zaheerabad Industrial Area breaks ground on schedule and whether the PM MITRA Park's job numbers hold up under independent audit.

nri_angle: Millions of Indian-Americans with roots in Telangana — especially the large Telugu community in cities like Houston, New Jersey, and the Bay Area — will watch closely as these projects reshape employment, healthcare, and logistics in their home state.
